create_invoice.description: Create a new invoice. Returns the invoice including `id` and `checkoutLink` to send to the payer. Omit amount for a top-up invoice. Use create_payment_request for a reusable request link instead.

checkout.description: Additional settings to customize the checkout flow

speedPolicy.description: This is a risk mitigation parameter for the merchant to configure how they want to fulfill orders depending on the number of block confirmations for the transaction made by the consumer on the selected cryptocurrency. `"HighSpeed"`: 0 confirmations (1 confirmation if RBF enabled in transaction) `"Me

paymentMethods.description: A specific set of payment methods to use for this invoice (ie. BTC, BTC-LightningNetwork). By default, select all payment methods enabled in the store.

defaultPaymentMethod.description: Default payment type for the invoice (e.g., BTC, BTC-LightningNetwork). Default payment method set for the store is used if this parameter is not specified.

lazyPaymentMethods.description: If true, payment methods are enabled individually upon user interaction in the invoice. Default to store's settings'

expirationMinutes.description: The number of minutes after which an invoice becomes expired. Defaults to the store's settings. (The default store settings is 15)

monitoringMinutes.description: The number of minutes after an invoice expired after which we are still monitoring for incoming payments. Defaults to the store's settings. (The default store settings is 1440, 1 day)

paymentTolerance.description: A percentage determining whether to count the invoice as paid when the invoice is paid within the specified margin of error. Defaults to the store's settings. (The default store settings is 0)

redirectURL.description: When the customer has paid the invoice, the URL where the customer will be redirected when clicking on the `return to store` button. You can use placeholders `{InvoiceId}` or `{OrderId}` in the URL, BTCPay Server will replace those with this invoice `id` or `metadata.orderId` respectively.

redirectAutomatically.description: When the customer has paid the invoice, and a `redirectURL` is set, the checkout is redirected to `redirectURL` automatically if `redirectAutomatically` is true. Defaults to the store's settings. (The default store settings is false)

defaultLanguage.description: The language code (eg. en-US, en, fr-FR...) of the language presented to your customer in the checkout page. BTCPay Server tries to match the best language available. If null or not set, will fallback on the store's default language. You can see the list of language codes with this operation.

receipt.description: Additional settings to customize the public receipt

enabled.description: A public page will be accessible once the invoice is settled. If null or unspecified, it will fallback to the store's settings. (The default store settings is true)

showQR.description: Show the QR code of the receipt in the public receipt page. If null or unspecified, it will fallback to the store's settings. (The default store setting is true)

showPayments.description: Show the payment list in the public receipt page. If null or unspecified, it will fallback to the store's settings. (The default store setting is true)

amount.description: The amount of the invoice. If null or unspecified, the invoice will be a top-up invoice. (ie. The invoice will consider any payment as a full payment)

currency.description: The currency of the invoice (if null, empty or unspecified, the currency will be the store's settings default)'

additional_search_terms.description: Additional search term to help you find this invoice via text search

refund_invoice.title: Refund invoice

name.description: Name of the pull payment (Default: 'Refund' followed by the invoice id)

payout_methods.description: The list of payout methods the refund can be claimed in. Available options can be queried from the `StorePaymentMethods_GetStorePaymentMethods` endpoint. If `null`, falls back to the deprecated single payout method, and if that is also `null`, to the default payout method of the original invoice.

refund_variant.description: * `RateThen`: Refund the crypto currency price, at the rate the invoice got paid. * `CurrentRate`: Refund the crypto currency price, at the current rate. *`Fiat`: Refund the invoice currency, at the rate when the refund will be sent. *`OverpaidAmount`: Refund the crypto currency amount that was overpaid. *`Custom`: Specify the amount, currency, and rate of the refund. (see `customAmount` and `customCurrency`)

subtract_percentage.description: Optional percentage by which to reduce the refund, e.g. as processing charge or to compensate for the mining fee.

custom_amount.description: The amount to refund if the `refundVariant` is `Custom`.

custom_currency.description: The currency to refund if the `refundVariant` is `Custom`

output.description: Pull payment for refunding the invoice
